verified.resolved_title: The UCL-Lancet Commission on Migration and Health: review of the state of progress
verified.note: DOI as listed (10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00494-0) is CORRECT and resolves via esearch to PMID 42314718, Lancet 2026 Jun 20;407(10547):2554-76 -- add the PMID, since the record only carried a bare DOI id. Abstract confirms the claim's substance: renews the call for (1) improved health-care access for refugees/migrants, (2) data systems with privacy safeguards, (3) research on climate-health impacts, (4) 'renewed focus on the political determinants of health outcomes for people on the move,' plus 'upholding the human rights and dignity of all.' Claim's 'inclusive services, equitable access, rights, dignity, privacy, political determinants' is a fair paraphrase. FIX = attach PMID 42314718 to the record; DOI itself needs no correction.

verified.resolved_title: Cultural competence education for health professionals
verified.note: Confirmed and strictly checked. Abstract states exactly: 'We included five RCTs involving 337 healthcare professionals and 8400 patients' -- matches '5 RCTs, 337 professionals, 8,400 patients' precisely. 'The quality of evidence for each outcome was judged to be low' -- matches 'low-quality evidence.' 'Involvement in care by non-Western patients... improved... in terms of mutual understanding' and improved 'health behaviour (client concordance with attendance)' -- matches 'some improvement in involvement/understanding.' 'Two trials... found no evidence of effect for treatment outcomes' -- matches 'no reliable clinical outcomes.' 'No study assessed adverse outcomes' appears verbatim twice (Results and Conclusions) -- matches 'adverse outcomes not assessed' exactly. All numeric and qualitative claims fully supported.

verified.resolved_title: Efficacy of culturally adapted interventions for common mental disorders in people of Chinese descent: a systematic review and meta-analysis
verified.note: DOI as listed is correct and resolves to PMID 37208113 (add PMID). Claim 'review/meta-analysis' is confirmed (67 RCTs, 6199 participants). However 'benefit population- and treatment-specific' overstates what the abstract says: interventions had a medium effect overall 'across all disorders' and the authors explicitly found 'no difference in efficacy between culturally modified interventions and culturally specific interventions... irrespective of adaptation types,' i.e. benefit was general, not shown to be adaptation-type-specific -- only 'considerable heterogeneity' in subgroup analyses is reported, which is weaker than a specificity claim. FIX = reword to 'medium overall effect on both self- and clinician-rated symptoms (Hedges' g ~0.75-0.77); no significant difference in efficacy between culturally modified vs culturally specific adaptations; heterogeneity across subgroups' and attach PMID 37208113.

verified.note: Placeholder DOI resolved via title/author esearch. Real citation: JAMA Netw Open. 2025 Feb 3;8(2):e2460551. doi: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.60551 (note year in DOI is 2024, not 2025 -- publication year is 2025). PMID 39969882. Retrospective cohort (Canadian Community Health Survey, 2003-2014), matches 'observational.' FIX = replace placeholder id with DOI 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.60551 and PMID 39969882; note the study population is Canadian (Canadian Community Health Survey), which the claim does not state but does not contradict either.

verified.resolved_title: Community-Level Social Support Infrastructure and Adult Onset of Major Depressive Disorder in a South Asian Postconflict Setting
verified.note: Placeholder DOI resolved via title/author/topic esearch. Real citation: JAMA Psychiatry. 2022 Mar 1;79(3):243-249. doi: 10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2021.4052 (DOI year is 2021, publication year 2022). PMID 35080609. Setting is western Chitwan valley, Nepal, longitudinal 2006-2015 -- matches 'Nepal longitudinal.' Exposure is the Small Farmers Development Program, described as building 'social capital and cohesion,' exogenously placed to 'simulate natural experiment conditions' -- matches 'community support structures (social capital/cohesion)... natural experiment.' Result: neighborhoods with the program had incident MDD of 7.4% vs 12.9% without (z=2.05, P=.04) -- supports 'associated with lower depression incidence.' One nuance: abstract frames sample as high-poverty/postconflict with Brahmin/Chhetri majority (44.7%) rather than explicitly 'ethnically diverse'; not contradicted but not directly stated either. FIX = replace placeholder id with DOI 10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2021.4052 and PMID 35080609.

verified.resolved_title: Effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a parenting programme to improve family wellbeing in England (TOGETHER): a multicentre, single-blind, randomised controlled trial
verified.note: Confirmed and strictly checked. Abstract: '674 participants were randomised to the waiting list control (n=314) and to the intervention group (n=360)' -- matches '674 participants' exactly. '420 [62%] from ethnic minority groups' -- matches '62% ethnic minority' exactly. 'delivered in weekly, 3-h group sessions over 13 weeks' -- matches '13 weeks' exactly. 'higher mental wellbeing at both post-intervention (mean difference 1.89...) and the 6-month follow-up (1.66...)' -- matches 'improved parental mental well-being post-programme and at 6 months' exactly. Note: PubMed lists this as 'single-blind, randomised controlled trial,' record's own trial name is SFSC (Strengthening Families, Strengthening Communities); claim's programme name is correct. All numeric and design claims fully supported.

overall_note: 9/9 records exist and are PubMed-indexed (Lancet x4 including 1 Commission report + 2-part Series, Cochrane, Lancet Psychiatry, JAMA Psychiatry, JAMA Network Open, Lancet Public Health) -- all in scope. 5 verdicts KEEP (25443490, 36502848, 36502849, 24793445, 41887826), all with claims fully supported by abstract text, and two (24793445 Horvat, 41887826 Watt/TOGETHER) strict-checked numerically with exact matches. 4 verdicts FIX, all for citation-metadata reasons rather than substantive misrepresentation: the Abubakar 2026 and Li 2023 items had correct DOIs but were missing PMIDs (42314718 and 37208113 respectively, both now resolved and claim-supported, though the Li claim's 'population- and treatment-specific' phrasing should be softened per the note above); the Reaume 2025 and Axinn 2022 items carried placeholder '.xxxx' DOIs that had to be resolved by title/author/topic search -- both resolved to real, claim-supporting articles (PMID 39969882 doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.60551; PMID 35080609 doi 10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2021.4052) and should have their id fields replaced with the correct DOI+PMID before publication. No record was dropped; no fabricated or unsupported numeric claim was found among the strict-checked items (Horvat and Watt/TOGETHER both matched their source abstracts exactly, digit for digit).
